data.narrative: The student executed a comprehensive, pattern-based review of AI-generated Team Collaboration code, proactively identifying an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability on the invitation endpoint prior to the break step. They demonstrated senior-level review thoroughness by auditing the code against the five systematic LLM failure categories, constructing a tightly-scoped fix prompt, and verifying both positive and negative authorization boundaries.

dimension_scores.observation: Constructed an authoritative, constraint-driven fix prompt naming the specific file, endpoint, exact database lookup table, role check, and 403 status code while explicitly prohibiting unrelated refactoring.
dimension_scores.evidence: Fix prompt explicitly required: team_members lookup for user_id = req.user.id AND team_id = req.params.teamId AND role IN ('admin', 'owner'), returning 403 with specific error message.

dimension_scores.observation: Systematically identified vulnerabilities across all 5 failure categories: IDOR, SQL injection in query interpolation, concurrent acceptance race conditions, orphaned state on email failure, and shallow happy-path unit tests.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documented 8 detailed findings with severity ratings and line-level evidence in progress/ai-augmented-engineering/module-04-review.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Executed pattern-based review rapidly, followed by surgical line-by-line verification on high-risk authorization logic, achieving 100% bug detection in a single iteration pass.
dimension_scores.evidence: Zero unnecessary prompt thrashing; fix landed cleanly on first generation with exact 403 authorization guard.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated why LLMs statistically omit per-resource authorization checks (autocomplete biases toward generic authentication rather than domain-specific tenancy logic) and instituted a permanent human-firewall checklist.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified IDOR as a consequence of pattern completion optimizing for standard auth middleware rather than contextual resource ownership.

dimension_scores.observation: The resulting codebase is robust, secure, and production-ready: parameterized queries, RBAC verification, compound uniqueness constraints, and automated negative test coverage.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verified both admin 201 Created and non-admin 403 Forbidden scenarios pass deterministically.

strengths: Human Firewall: caught critical IDOR and SQL injection vulnerabilities before deployment
High-fidelity prompt specification: prevented AI placeholder code ('TODO: check admin') by specifying exact table names, parameters, and return payloads
Dual boundary verification: tested both positive (admin) and negative (non-admin) access controls
data.recommendation: In Module 05, apply this review rigor to multi-agent parallel generation pipelines to catch interface divergence between agents.
